speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate the cause of your systemic hypertension. How old are you, and have you noticed any symptoms like headaches, blurred vision, or chest pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since you are asymptomatic, I need to determine if this is essential hypertension or secondary to an underlying condition. Please tell me, have there been any recent episodes of swelling in your legs, difficulty breathing, or sudden weight gain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta.

The finding of isolated hypertension in the right upper extremity in a young child is highly suggestive of coarctation of the aorta. REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram to visualize the aortic arch and ductus arteriosus.
